passages.text: Now Ben-hadad king of Aram assembled his entire army. Accompanied by thirty-two kings with their horses and chariots, he marched up, besieged Samaria, and waged war against it.
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
He gathered his entire army.
Thirty-two kings went with him.
They brought horses and chariots.
Ben-hadad marched to Samaria.
He surrounded the city.
He fought against Samaria.
passages.original: וּבֶן־ הֲדַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֗ם קָבַץ֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ חֵיל֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וּשְׁנַ֥יִם מֶ֛לֶךְ אִתּ֖וֹ וְס֣וּס וָרָ֑כֶב וַיַּ֗עַל וַיָּ֙צַר֙ עַל־ שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then he sent messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel, saying, “This is what Ben-hadad says: ‘Your silver and gold are mine, and your best wives and children are mine!’ ”
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
He sent messengers into the city.
He sent them to Ahab, the king of Israel.
The messengers spoke to Ahab.
They said, “This is what Ben-hadad says.”
Ben-hadad said, “Your silver is mine.”
He said, “Your gold is mine.”
He said, “Your best wives are mine.”
He said, “Your best children are mine.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח מַלְאָכִ֛ים אֶל־ אַחְאָ֥ב מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הָעִֽירָה׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר בֶּן־ הֲדַ֔ד כַּסְפְּךָ֥ וּֽזְהָבְךָ֖ לִֽי־ ה֑וּא וְנָשֶׁ֧יךָ וּבָנֶ֛יךָ הַטּוֹבִ֖ים לִי־ הֵֽם׃

passages.text: And the king of Israel replied, “Just as you say, my lord the king: I am yours, along with all that I have.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke.
He answered Ben-hadad, king of Aram.
He said, "Yes, my lord the king."
"I belong to you."
"All that I have belongs to you."
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַן מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר כִּדְבָרְךָ֖ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ לְךָ֥ אֲנִ֖י וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁר־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: The messengers came back and said, “This is what Ben-hadad says: ‘I have sent to you to demand your silver, your gold, your wives, and your children.
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
He sent messengers to Ahab, the king of Israel.
The messengers returned to Ahab.
They spoke to Ahab.
They said, “This is what Ben-hadad says.”
Ben-hadad said, “I have sent a message to you.”
He said, “Give me your silver.”
He said, “Give me your gold.”
He said, “Give me your wives.”
He said, “Give me your children.”
passages.original: וַיָּשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֥ר בֶּן־ הֲדַ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר כִּֽי־ שָׁלַ֤חְתִּי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כַּסְפְּךָ֧ וּזְהָבְךָ֛ וְנָשֶׁ֥יךָ וּבָנֶ֖יךָ לִ֥י תִתֵּֽן׃

passages.text: But about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to search your palace and the houses of your servants. They will seize and carry away all that is precious to you.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
He threatened the king of Israel.
He said, “About this time tomorrow, I will act.”
“I will send my servants to you.”
“They will search your palace.”
“They will also search the houses of your servants.”
“They will take everything that is precious to you.”
“They will seize these things and carry them away.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י׀ אִם־ כָּעֵ֣ת מָחָ֗ר אֶשְׁלַ֤ח אֶת־ עֲבָדַי֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְחִפְּשׂוּ֙ אֶת־ בֵּ֣יתְךָ֔ וְאֵ֖ת בָּתֵּ֣י עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ וְהָיָה֙ כָּל־ מַחְמַ֣ד עֵינֶ֔יךָ יָשִׂ֥ימוּ בְיָדָ֖ם וְלָקָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, “Please take note and see that this man is looking for trouble, for when he demanded my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, I did not deny him.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel called all the elders of the land.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Please pay attention.
See what is happening.
This man is seeking evil against us.
He sent messengers to me.
He demanded my wives.
He demanded my children.
He demanded my silver.
He demanded my gold.
I did not refuse him.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְכָל־ זִקְנֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ דְּעֽוּ־ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ כִּ֥י רָעָ֖ה זֶ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֑שׁ כִּֽי־ שָׁלַ֨ח אֵלַ֜י לְנָשַׁ֤י וּלְבָנַי֙ וּלְכַסְפִּ֣י וְלִזְהָבִ֔י וְלֹ֥א מָנַ֖עְתִּי מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: And the elders and the people all said, “Do not listen to him or consent to his terms.”
passages.sermon:
The elders of Israel spoke to the king.
The people of Israel also spoke to the king.
They said, “Do not listen to Ben-hadad.”
They said, “Do not agree to his demands.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלָ֛יו כָּל־ הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים וְכָל־ הָעָ֑ם אַל־ תִּשְׁמַ֖ע וְל֥וֹא תֹאבֶֽה׃

passages.text: So Ahab answered the messengers of Ben-hadad, “Tell my lord the king, ‘All that you demanded of your servant the first time I will do, but this thing I cannot do.’ ” So the messengers departed and relayed the message to Ben-hadad.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Ben-hadad sent messengers to Ahab.
Ahab spoke to the messengers of Ben-hadad.
Ahab said, “Tell your master, the king.
I will do everything you demanded from me at first.
But I cannot do this new thing you ask.”
The messengers left.
The messengers gave Ben-hadad Ahab’s answer.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר לְמַלְאֲכֵ֣י בֶן־ הֲדַ֗ד אִמְר֞וּ לַֽאדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁלַ֨חְתָּ אֶל־ עַבְדְּךָ֤ בָרִֽאשֹׁנָה֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה וְהַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לֹ֥א אוּכַ֖ל לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים וַיְשִׁבֻ֖הוּ דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: Then Ben-hadad sent another message to Ahab: “May the gods deal with me, and ever so severely, if enough dust remains of Samaria for each of my men to have a handful.”
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Ben-hadad sent a message to Ahab, the king of Israel.
Ben-hadad said, “May the gods punish me if I am not telling the truth.”
Ben-hadad said, “May the gods punish me even more if I fail.”
Ben-hadad said, “There will not be enough dust left in Samaria for each of my soldiers to have a handful.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֵלָיו֙ בֶּן־ הֲדַ֔ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כֹּֽה־ יַעֲשׂ֥וּן לִ֛י אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֑פוּ אִם־ יִשְׂפֹּק֙ עֲפַ֣ר שֹׁמְר֔וֹן לִשְׁעָלִ֕ים לְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרַגְלָֽי׃

passages.text: And the king of Israel replied, “Tell him: ‘The one putting on his armor should not boast like one taking it off.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke.
He replied to Ben-hadad’s message.
He said, “Tell him this.”
A man who puts on his armor should not boast.
A man who takes off his armor after battle can boast.
Do not boast before the battle is won.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַן מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דַּבְּר֔וּ אַל־ יִתְהַלֵּ֥ל חֹגֵ֖ר כִּמְפַתֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: Ben-hadad received this message while he and the kings were drinking in their tents, and he said to his servants, “Take your positions.” So they stationed themselves against the city.
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
He received a message from Ahab, the king of Israel.
Ben-hadad was drinking in his tent.
Other kings were with him.
They were also drinking.
Their tents were outside the city.
Ben-hadad spoke to his servants.
He said, "Take your positions."
The servants obeyed.
They took their positions against the city.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וְה֥וּא שֹׁתֶ֛ה ה֥וּא וְהַמְּלָכִ֖ים בַּסֻּכּ֑וֹת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־ עֲבָדָיו֙ שִׂ֔ימוּ וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ עַל־ הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Meanwhile a prophet approached Ahab king of Israel and declared, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Do you see this entire great army? Behold, I will deliver it into your hand this very day, and you will know that I am the LORD.’ ”
passages.sermon:
A prophet came to Ahab.
Ahab was the king of Israel.
The prophet spoke to Ahab.
The prophet said, “This is what the LORD says.”
The prophet asked, “Do you see this great army?”
The LORD says, “I will give this army into your hand today.”
The LORD says, “You will know that I am the LORD.”
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ נָבִ֣יא אֶחָ֗ד נִגַּשׁ֮ אֶל־ אַחְאָ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הְֽרָאִ֔יתָ אֵ֛ת כָּל־ הֶהָמ֥וֹן הַגָּד֖וֹל הַזֶּ֑ה הִנְנִ֨י נֹתְנ֤וֹ בְיָֽדְךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְיָדַעְתָּ֖ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “By whom?” Ahab asked. And the prophet replied, “This is what the LORD says: ‘By the young officers of the district governors.’ ” “Who will start the battle?” asked Ahab. “You will,” answered the prophet.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the king of Israel.
A prophet spoke to Ahab.
Ahab asked, “By whom will this happen?”
The prophet answered, “The LORD says, ‘By the young officers of the district governors.’”
Ahab asked, “Who will begin the battle?”
The prophet answered, “You will.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַחְאָב֙ בְּמִ֔י וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּנַעֲרֵ֖י שָׂרֵ֣י הַמְּדִינ֑וֹת וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מִֽי־ יֶאְסֹ֥ר הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: So Ahab assembled the young officers of the district governors, and there were 232 men. And after them, he assembled the rest of the Israelite troops, 7,000 in all.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Ahab gathered the young officers.
These young officers served under the district governors.
There were 232 young officers.
After this, Ahab gathered all the rest of the Israelite soldiers.
There were 7,000 Israelite soldiers.
passages.original: וַיִּפְקֹ֗ד אֶֽת־ נַעֲרֵי֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הַמְּדִינ֔וֹת וַיִּהְי֕וּ מָאתַ֖יִם שְׁנַ֣יִם וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֑ים וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם פָּקַ֧ד אֶת־ כָּל־ הָעָ֛ם כָּל־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שִׁבְעַ֥ת אֲלָפִֽים׃

passages.text: They marched out at noon while Ben-hadad and the 32 kings allied with him were in their tents getting drunk.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Ben-hadad had thirty-two kings allied with him.
The young officers of the district governors marched out at noon.
Ben-hadad and the thirty-two allied kings were in their tents.
They were drinking.
They were getting drunk.
passages.original: וַיֵּצְא֖וּ בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם וּבֶן־ הֲדַד֩ שֹׁתֶ֨ה שִׁכּ֜וֹר בַּסֻּכּ֗וֹת ה֧וּא וְהַמְּלָכִ֛ים שְׁלֹשִֽׁים־ וּשְׁנַ֥יִם מֶ֖לֶךְ עֹזֵ֥ר אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And the young officers of the district governors marched out first. Now Ben-hadad had sent out scouts, who reported to him, “Men are marching out of Samaria.”
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Ahab assembled his army in Samaria.
He chose young officers from the district governors.
These young officers marched out first.
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Ben-hadad had allied kings with him.
Ben-hadad sent out scouts.
The scouts returned to Ben-hadad.
They reported to him.
They said, “Men are marching out of Samaria.”
passages.original: וַיֵּצְא֗וּ נַעֲרֵ֛י שָׂרֵ֥י הַמְּדִינ֖וֹת בָּרִֽאשֹׁנָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח בֶּן־ הֲדַ֗ד וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֲנָשִׁ֕ים יָצְא֖וּ מִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: “If they have marched out in peace,” he said, “take them alive. Even if they have marched out for war, take them alive.”
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
He spoke to his men.
He said, "If the men from Samaria have come out in peace, take them alive."
He also said, "If they have come out for war, take them alive."
He commanded his men to capture the Israelites alive, no matter their reason for coming out.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר אִם־ לְשָׁל֥וֹם יָצָ֖אוּ תִּפְשׂ֣וּם חַיִּ֑ים וְאִ֧ם לְמִלְחָמָ֛ה יָצָ֖אוּ חַיִּ֥ים תִּפְשֽׂוּם׃

passages.text: Meanwhile, these young officers of the district governors marched out of the city, with the army behind them, and each one struck down his opponent. So the Arameans fled, with the Israelites in pursuit. But Ben-hadad king of Aram escaped on horseback with the cavalry.
passages.sermon:
The young officers served the district governors of Israel.
They marched out of the city.
The Israelite army followed behind them.
Each young officer struck down his opponent.
The Aramean soldiers saw this.
The Arameans fled from the Israelites.
The Israelites chased after the Arameans.
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Ben-hadad escaped on horseback.
The cavalry escaped with Ben-hadad.
passages.original: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ יָצְא֣וּ מִן־ הָעִ֔יר נַעֲרֵ֖י שָׂרֵ֣י הַמְּדִינ֑וֹת וְהַחַ֖יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃ וַיַּכּוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אִישׁ֔וֹ וַיָּנֻ֣סוּ אֲרָ֔ם וַֽיִּרְדְּפֵ֖ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּמָּלֵ֗ט בֶּן־ הֲדַד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם עַל־ ס֖וּס וּפָרָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Then the king of Israel marched out and attacked the horses and chariots, inflicting a great slaughter on the Arameans.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel led his army.
He marched out from the city.
He attacked the horses of the Arameans.
He attacked the chariots of the Arameans.
He struck the Aramean army.
He caused a great defeat for the Arameans.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־ הַסּ֖וּס וְאֶת־ הָרָ֑כֶב וְהִכָּ֥ה בַאֲרָ֖ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃

passages.text: Afterward, the prophet approached the king of Israel and said, “Go and strengthen your position, and take note what you must do, for in the spring the king of Aram will come up against you.”
passages.sermon:
A prophet came to the king of Israel.
The prophet spoke to the king.
He said, “Go and make yourself strong.
Pay attention to what you must do.
You must prepare.
In the spring, the king of Aram will attack you.”
passages.original: וַיִּגַּ֤שׁ הַנָּבִיא֙ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ לֵ֣ךְ הִתְחַזַּ֔ק וְדַ֥ע וּרְאֵ֖ה אֵ֣ת אֲשֶֽׁר־ תַּעֲשֶׂ֑ה כִּ֚י לִתְשׁוּבַ֣ת הַשָּׁנָ֔ה מֶ֥לֶךְ אֲרָ֖ם עֹלֶ֥ה עָלֶֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: Meanwhile, the servants of the king of Aram said to him, “Their gods are gods of the hills. That is why they prevailed over us. Instead, we should fight them on the plains; surely then we will prevail.
passages.sermon:
The servants of the king of Aram spoke to him.
They said, "The Israelites have gods of the hills.
That is why the Israelites were stronger than us.
Let us fight the Israelites on the plains instead.
Then we will surely be stronger than they are."
passages.original: וְעַבְדֵ֨י מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֜ם אָמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָרִים֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם עַל־ כֵּ֖ן חָזְק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְאוּלָ֗ם נִלָּחֵ֤ם אִתָּם֙ בַּמִּישׁ֔וֹר אִם־ לֹ֥א נֶחֱזַ֖ק מֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So do this: Dismiss all the kings from their positions and replace them with other officers.
passages.sermon:
The servants of the king of Aram spoke to him.
They gave him advice.
They said, “Remove all the kings from their positions.
Take each king away from his place.
Appoint other officers instead of them.
Put new commanders in their places.”
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה עֲשֵׂ֑ה הָסֵ֤ר הַמְּלָכִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֔וֹ וְשִׂ֥ים פַּח֖וֹת תַּחְתֵּיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And you must raise an army like the one you have lost—horse for horse and chariot for chariot—so we can fight the Israelites on the plain, where we will surely prevail.” And the king approved their plan and acted accordingly.
passages.sermon:
The king of Aram listened to his servants.
They told him to prepare for battle against Israel.
They said, “Raise an army like the one you lost.
Replace every lost soldier with a new one.
Replace every lost horse with a new horse.
Replace every lost chariot with a new chariot.
We will fight Israel on the plain.
We will be stronger than them there.”
The king agreed with their advice.
He did everything they said.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה תִֽמְנֶה־ לְךָ֣׀ חַ֡יִל כַּחַיִל֩ הַנֹּפֵ֨ל מֵאוֹתָ֜ךְ וְס֣וּס כַּסּ֣וּס׀ וְרֶ֣כֶב כָּרֶ֗כֶב וְנִֽלָּחֲמָ֤ה אוֹתָם֙ בַּמִּישׁ֔וֹר אִם־ לֹ֥א נֶחֱזַ֖ק מֵהֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע לְקֹלָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ כֵּֽן׃פ

passages.text: In the spring, Ben-hadad mobilized the Arameans and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Spring came.
Ben-hadad gathered the army of Aram.
He led the Arameans to Aphek.
They went to fight against Israel.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ לִתְשׁוּבַ֣ת הַשָּׁנָ֔ה וַיִּפְקֹ֥ד בֶּן־ הֲדַ֖ד אֶת־ אֲרָ֑ם וַיַּ֣עַל אֲפֵ֔קָה לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: The Israelites also mobilized, gathered supplies, and marched out to meet them. The Israelites camped before them like two small flocks of goats, while the Arameans covered the countryside.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were God's chosen people.
The Israelites gathered together.
They prepared their supplies.
They marched out to face the Arameans.
The Israelites set up camp in front of the Arameans.
Their camp looked small, like two little flocks of goats.
The Arameans were their enemies.
The Arameans filled the whole land.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הָתְפָּקְדוּ֙ וְכָלְכְּל֔וּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לִקְרָאתָ֑ם וַיַּחֲנ֨וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל נֶגְדָּ֗ם כִּשְׁנֵי֙ חֲשִׂפֵ֣י עִזִּ֔ים וַאֲרָ֖ם מִלְא֥וּ אֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Then the man of God approached the king of Israel and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because the Arameans think the LORD is a god of the hills and not of the valleys, I will deliver all this great army into your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’ ”
passages.sermon:
A man of God came to the king of Israel.
He spoke to the king.
He said, “This is what the LORD says.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The Arameans said, ‘The LORD is only a god of the hills.
He is not a god of the valleys.’
Because they said this, I will act.
I will give this great army into your hand.
You will defeat them.
Then you will know that I am the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיִּגַּ֞שׁ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיֹּ֜אמֶר כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה יַ֠עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמְר֤וּ אֲרָם֙ אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָרִים֙ יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ אֱלֹהֵ֥י עֲמָקִ֖ים ה֑וּא וְ֠נָתַתִּי אֶת־ כָּל־ הֶהָמ֨וֹן הַגָּ֤דוֹל הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: For seven days the armies camped opposite each other, and on the seventh day the battle ensued, and the Israelites struck down the Arameans—a hundred thousand foot soldiers in one day.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were God's chosen people.
The Arameans were their enemies.
The Israelite army camped across from the Aramean army.
They stayed like this for seven days.
On the seventh day, the battle began.
The Israelites fought the Arameans.
The Israelites killed one hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day.
passages.original: וַֽיַּחֲנ֧וּ אֵ֦לֶּה נֹ֥כַח אֵ֖לֶּה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וַתִּקְרַב֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַיַּכּ֨וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל אֶת־ אֲרָ֛ם מֵאָה־ אֶ֥לֶף רַגְלִ֖י בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: The rest of them fled into the city of Aphek, where the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the remaining men. Ben-hadad also fled to the city and hid in an inner room.
passages.sermon:
The Aramean army fought against Israel.
Some Aramean soldiers survived the battle.
These remaining soldiers ran away.
They fled to the city of Aphek.
A wall in the city collapsed.
The wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the soldiers who had fled.
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Ben-hadad also escaped to Aphek.
He entered the city.
He hid inside an inner room.
passages.original: וַיָּנֻ֨סוּ הַנּוֹתָרִ֥ים׀ אֲפֵקָה֮ אֶל־ הָעִיר֒ וַתִּפֹּל֙ הַחוֹמָ֔ה עַל־ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ הַנּוֹתָרִ֑ים וּבֶן־ הֲדַ֣ד נָ֔ס וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל־ הָעִ֖יר חֶ֥דֶר בְּחָֽדֶר׃ס

passages.text: Then the servants of Ben-hadad said to him, “Look now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful. Let us go out to the king of Israel with sackcloth around our waists and ropes around our heads. Perhaps he will spare your life.”
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
His servants spoke to him.
They said, “We have heard something important.
The kings of Israel are merciful.
They show kindness.
Let us do something to show we are humble.
Let us put sackcloth around our waists.
Let us put ropes on our heads.
Let us go out to the king of Israel.
Maybe he will let you live.
Maybe he will spare your life.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָיו֮ עֲבָדָיו֒ הִנֵּֽה־ נָ֣א שָׁמַ֔עְנוּ כִּ֗י מַלְכֵי֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּֽי־ מַלְכֵ֥י חֶ֖סֶד הֵ֑ם נָשִׂ֣ימָה נָּא֩ שַׂקִּ֨ים בְּמָתְנֵ֜ינוּ וַחֲבָלִ֣ים בְּרֹאשֵׁ֗נוּ וְנֵצֵא֙ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אוּלַ֖י יְחַיֶּ֥ה אֶת־ נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: So with sackcloth around their waists and ropes around their heads, they went to the king of Israel and said, “Your servant Ben-hadad says, ‘Please spare my life.’ ” And the king answered, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”
passages.sermon:
The servants of Ben-hadad put sackcloth around their waists.
They put ropes on their heads.
They went to the king of Israel.
They spoke to the king of Israel.
They said, “Your servant Ben-hadad says, ‘Please spare my life.’”
The king of Israel answered them.
He said, “Is he still alive?”
He said, “He is my brother.”
passages.original: וַיַּחְגְּרוּ֩ שַׂקִּ֨ים בְּמָתְנֵיהֶ֜ם וַחֲבָלִ֣ים בְּרָאשֵׁיהֶ֗ם וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ עַבְדְּךָ֧ בֶן־ הֲדַ֛ד אָמַ֖ר תְּחִֽי־ נָ֣א נַפְשִׁ֑י וַיֹּ֛אמֶר הַעוֹדֶ֥נּוּ חַ֖י אָחִ֥י הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Now the men were looking for a sign of hope, and they quickly grasped at this word and replied, “Yes, your brother Ben-hadad.” “Go and get him!” said the king. Then Ben-hadad came out, and Ahab had him come up into his chariot.
passages.sermon:
The men served Ben-hadad.
They looked for a sign of hope from King Ahab of Israel.
Ahab called Ben-hadad his brother.
The men quickly took hold of this word.
They answered Ahab, “Your brother is Ben-hadad.”
Ahab said, “Go. Bring him.”
Ben-hadad came out to Ahab.
Ahab brought Ben-hadad up into his chariot.
passages.original: וְהָאֲנָשִׁים֩ יְנַחֲשׁ֨וּ וַֽיְמַהֲר֜וּ וַיַּחְלְט֣וּ הֲמִמֶּ֗נּוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אָחִ֣יךָ בֶן־ הֲדַ֔ד וַיֹּ֖אמֶר בֹּ֣אוּ קָחֻ֑הוּ וַיֵּצֵ֤א אֵלָיו֙ בֶּן־ הֲדַ֔ד וַֽיַּעֲלֵ֖הוּ עַל־ הַמֶּרְכָּבָֽה׃

passages.text: Ben-hadad said to him, “I will restore the cities my father took from your father; you may set up your own marketplaces in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria.” “By this treaty I release you,” Ahab replied. So he made a treaty with him and sent him away.
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Ben-hadad spoke to Ahab.
Ben-hadad said, “I will return the cities my father took from your father.”
Ben-hadad said, “You may set up marketplaces for yourself in Damascus.”
Ben-hadad said, “My father set up marketplaces in Samaria.”
Ahab answered Ben-hadad.
Ahab said, “I will release you by this treaty.”
Ahab made a treaty with Ben-hadad.
Ahab sent Ben-hadad away.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֡יו הֶעָרִ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־ לָֽקַח־ אָבִי֩ מֵאֵ֨ת אָבִ֜יךָ אָשִׁ֗יב וְ֠חוּצוֹת תָּשִׂ֨ים לְךָ֤ בְדַמֶּ֙שֶׂק֙ כַּאֲשֶׁר־ שָׂ֤ם אָבִי֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַאֲנִ֖י בַּבְּרִ֣ית אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֑ךָּ וַיִּכְרָת־ ל֥וֹ בְרִ֖ית וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵֽהוּ׃ס

passages.text: Meanwhile, by the word of the LORD, one of the sons of the prophets said to his companion, “Strike me, please!” But the man refused to strike him.
passages.sermon:
One man belonged to the sons of the prophets.
He spoke to his companion.
He spoke by the word of the LORD.
He said, “Strike me, please!”
The companion refused to strike him.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ישׁ אֶחָ֜ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֗ים אָמַ֧ר אֶל־ רֵעֵ֛הוּ בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה הַכֵּ֣ינִי נָ֑א וַיְמָאֵ֥ן הָאִ֖ישׁ לְהַכֹּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the prophet said to him, “Because you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD, as soon as you depart from me a lion will kill you.” And when he left, a lion found him and killed him.
passages.sermon:
A prophet spoke to a man who refused his request.
The prophet said, “You did not obey the voice of the LORD.
You will leave me now.
A lion will kill you.”
The man left the prophet.
A lion found the man.
The lion killed him.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ שָׁמַ֙עְתָּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה הִנְּךָ֤ הוֹלֵךְ֙ מֵֽאִתִּ֔י וְהִכְּךָ֖ הָאַרְיֵ֑ה וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ מֵֽאֶצְל֔וֹ וַיִּמְצָאֵ֥הוּ הָאַרְיֵ֖ה וַיַּכֵּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Then the prophet found another man and said, “Strike me, please!” So the man struck him and wounded him, and the prophet went and waited on the road for the king, disguising himself with a bandage over his eyes.
passages.sermon:
A prophet was one of the sons of the prophets.
He found another man.
The prophet said, “Strike me, please.”
The man struck the prophet.
The man wounded the prophet.
The prophet went to the road.
The prophet waited for the king on the road.
The prophet disguised himself.
He put a bandage over his eyes.
passages.original: וַיִּמְצָא֙ אִ֣ישׁ אַחֵ֔ר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הַכֵּ֣ינִי נָ֑א וַיַּכֵּ֥הוּ הָאִ֖ישׁ הַכֵּ֥ה וּפָצֹֽעַ׃ וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־ הַדָּ֑רֶךְ וַיִּתְחַפֵּ֥שׂ בָּאֲפֵ֖ר עַל־ עֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: As the king passed by, he cried out to the king: “Your servant had marched out into the middle of the battle, when suddenly a man came over with a captive and told me, ‘Guard this man! If he goes missing for any reason, your life will be exchanged for his life, or you will weigh out a talent of silver.’
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel passed by on the road.
A man cried out to the king.
The man said, “I am your servant.
I went out into the middle of the battle.
Suddenly, another man came to me.
He brought a captive to me.
He said, ‘Guard this man.
If this man goes missing for any reason, you will pay with your own life.
Or you must pay a talent of silver.’”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ עֹבֵ֔ר וְה֖וּא צָעַ֣ק אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֜אמֶר עַבְדְּךָ֣׀ יָצָ֣א בְקֶֽרֶב־ הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְהִנֵּֽה־ אִ֨ישׁ סָ֜ר וַיָּבֵ֧א אֵלַ֣י אִ֗ישׁ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ שְׁמֹר֙ אֶת־ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה אִם־ הִפָּקֵד֙ יִפָּקֵ֔ד וְהָיְתָ֤ה נַפְשְׁךָ֙ תַּ֣חַת נַפְשׁ֔וֹ א֥וֹ כִכַּר־ כֶּ֖סֶף תִּשְׁקֽוֹל׃

passages.text: But while your servant was busy here and there, the man disappeared.” And the king of Israel said to him, “So shall your judgment be; you have pronounced it on yourself.”
passages.sermon:
The servant spoke to the king of Israel.
The servant said, “I was busy here and there.
The man I was supposed to guard disappeared.”
The king of Israel answered the servant.
The king said, “This is your judgment.
You have decided it for yourself.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י עַבְדְּךָ֗ עֹשֵׂ֥ה הֵ֛נָּה וָהֵ֖נָּה וְה֣וּא אֵינֶ֑נּוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֧יו מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל כֵּ֥ן מִשְׁפָּטֶ֖ךָ אַתָּ֥ה חָרָֽצְתָּ׃

passages.text: Then the prophet quickly removed the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him as one of the prophets.
passages.sermon:
A prophet stood before the king of Israel.
The prophet wore a bandage over his eyes.
The prophet quickly removed the bandage from his eyes.
The king of Israel looked at the man.
The king of Israel recognized the man.
The king of Israel saw that the man was one of the prophets.
passages.original: וַיְמַהֵ֕ר וַיָּ֙סַר֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֲפֵ֔ר מֵעַל עֵינָ֑יו וַיַּכֵּ֤ר אֹתוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י מֵֽהַנְּבִאִ֖ים הֽוּא׃

passages.text: And the prophet said to the king, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because you have let slip from your hand the man I had devoted to destruction, your life will be exchanged for his life, and your people for his people.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The prophet spoke to the king of Israel.
The prophet said, “This is what the LORD says.”
The LORD had chosen a man to be destroyed.
The king let this man escape.
The LORD said, “You let this man go free.”
“Because of this, your life will be taken instead of his life.”
“Your people will be taken instead of his people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה יַ֛עַן שִׁלַּ֥חְתָּ אֶת־ אִישׁ־ חֶרְמִ֖י מִיָּ֑ד וְהָיְתָ֤ה נַפְשְׁךָ֙ תַּ֣חַת נַפְשׁ֔וֹ וְעַמְּךָ֖ תַּ֥חַת עַמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Sullen and angry, the king of Israel went home to Samaria.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel felt sullen.
He felt angry.
He went to his house.
He entered his home in Samaria.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַל־ בֵּית֖וֹ סַ֣ר וְזָעֵ֑ף וַיָּבֹ֖א שֹׁמְרֽוֹנָה׃פ
